questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The hybridisation of phosphorous in ${PO}_{4}^{3 -}$& is
questions.solution:
The structure of ${PO}_{4}^{3 -}$ is as follows

In the given molecule, The P atom have 5 valence electrons. The hybridization can be determined by the number of sigma bonds and the number of lone pair.

As phosphorous central atom forms four $\left(4\right)$ sigma bonds and has no lone pair of electrons. It uses four hybrid orbital and thus, hybridisation of $p$-atom is ${sp}^{3}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The most acidic oxide for nitrogen is
questions.solution:
The acidic nature of the oxides of nitrogen can be determined by the strength of the acid formed by the nitrogen oxide in water.&

More higher be the $( + ) ve$ oxidation number of $N$-atom in its oxide more acidic be the nature of oxide. Thus ${N}_{2}{O}_{5}$, is most acidic oxide.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Strong reducing behaviour of $\mathrm{H}_{3} \mathrm{PO}_{2}$ is due to
options: presence of one $-\mathrm{OH}$ group and two $\mathrm{P}-\mathrm{H}$ bonds
high electron gain enthalpy of phosphorus
presence of two -OH groups and one $\mathrm{P}-\mathrm{H}$ bond
questions.solution: The acids which contain $\mathrm{P}-\mathrm{H}$ bond have strong reducing properties. Thus $\mathrm{H}_{3} \mathrm{PO}_{2}$ acid is good reducing agent as it contains two P-H bonds. For example, it reduces $\mathrm{AgNO}_{3}$ to metallic silver.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is less acidic among the given halogen compounds?
questions.solution: Due to stronger-I-effect of $\mathrm{F}$ than that of Cl, $\mathrm{CHF}_{3}$ should be more acidic than $\mathrm{CHCl}_{3}.$ But actually reverse is true. This is due to : $\mathrm{CCl}_{3}^{-}$ left after the removal of a proton from $\mathrm{CHCl}_{3}$ is stabilised due to presence of $d$ -orbitals in Cl than: $\mathrm{CF}_{3}^{-}$ left after the removal of a proton from $\mathrm{CHF}_{3}$ which is not stabilised due to the absence of $d$ -orbitals on $\mathrm{F}$.
